h1: A career in brewery quality control
title: Brewery Quality Control Careers in India | Craft Beer School
desc: What brewery quality control staff do, the tests they run, the background that gets you in and how the role grows in Indian breweries large and small.
teaser: Every tank, can and keg passes through someone's hands before it is released. That someone has an interesting job.
standfirst: Quality control is the part of a brewery that decides whether a beer is fit to leave the building. It suits people with a science background who like evidence more than opinions.
sections: What quality control people actually do

A brewery QC role sits between the brewers and the customer. You take samples at set points, measure them, compare the results with the specification and decide whether the beer moves on. When something drifts you trace it back: which tank, which batch of yeast, which shift.

In a large brewery that work is split across a lab team with defined jobs. In a craft brewery or brewpub the QC person may also be the assistant brewer, doing the tests between brew days. Both are real careers. The first gives you depth and good equipment. The second gives you range and a voice in decisions.

The daily routine is built around a handful of measurements:

  • Gravity during fermentation, to track how far the yeast has got and when the beer has finished.
  • pH of mash, wort and finished beer.
  • Carbon dioxide in bright beer and packaged product, so every can pours the same.
  • Dissolved oxygen after packaging. Many breweries aim to keep it well under 100 parts per billion, because oxygen is what makes beer taste stale.
  • Microbiology: plating samples to check for bacteria and wild yeast.
  • Sensory: tasting each batch against its standard before release.

Bigger labs add colour, bitterness, alcohol and haze stability. Our guide to a QC lab on a budget shows what a small brewery can do with modest kit.
The background that gets you hired

Most people who move into brewery QC come from microbiology, biotechnology, food technology or chemistry. Lab habits matter more than brewing experience at the start: clean technique, careful records and the patience to repeat a test when a number looks odd.

What a science graduate usually lacks is the brewing context. You can plate a sample perfectly and still not know why a lactic acid bacterium in a lager tank is an emergency while the same organism in a sour beer is the plan. That gap closes faster if you learn the brewing process before you learn the brewery's paperwork.
Why sensory matters as much as the lab

Instruments miss things a trained taster picks up in seconds. Diacetyl, the butterscotch fault, is the classic example: a beer can look fine on every routine number and still taste wrong. QC people who can taste reliably become very valuable, because they catch a fault before it reaches a hundred kegs.

Learn the common beer off flavours early and taste them deliberately. Spiked samples are the standard way to train.
Where the jobs are in India

Large breweries employ the most QC staff, often at plants outside the big cities, with structured shifts and clear grades. Craft breweries and contract brewers hire fewer people but are growing their quality work as their beers travel further and sit longer in warm shops.

The Indian cold chain is the hidden reason QC matters so much here. A beer that leaves the brewery clean can arrive stale after days in a hot truck. Breweries that sell outside their own taproom need someone who can measure that risk and argue for fixing it.
A day in a brewery lab

A typical shift starts with sampling. You walk the cellar with a tray of sterile bottles, drawing from fermenters and bright tanks at their scheduled points, labelling each one carefully. Back in the lab you run gravity and pH first, because the brewers are waiting for those numbers to decide whether to cool a tank or move it.

Mid-shift is for the slower work: plating microbiology samples, reading plates incubated over previous days, measuring carbonation on the packaging line. Then the tasting panel, if one is scheduled. The day ends with records. Every result goes into a log against its specification. Anything outside it is flagged to the head brewer before you leave.

It is careful, repetitive work. The interesting days are the ones when a number is wrong and you have to find out why.

A typical path runs from lab analyst to senior analyst, then QC or quality assurance lead, then head of quality across a site. Some people move sideways into brewing, because they already understand the process better than most. Others go into supplier quality, sensory management or food safety systems. Professional exams from bodies such as the Institute of Brewing and Distilling help at the later steps.
faqs: Do I need a brewing qualification for a QC job?
Not at entry level. A science degree and good lab habits usually get you in. Brewing knowledge and sensory skills are what move you up.
What is the difference between QC and QA in a brewery?
Quality control tests the product and catches problems. Quality assurance designs the systems and procedures that stop problems happening in the first place.
Is brewery QC a good career for a microbiology graduate?
It is one of the most natural fits. Contamination is the risk breweries fear most and microbiologists are trained to find it.
